A total of 12 teams competed in the tournament. [[Sporting Cristal]] won its fifteenth Primera División title after beating [[Cienciano]] in the season final.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/peru05.html Rsssf.org Peru 2005][https://www.clubsportingcristal.pe/historia/19-historia/campeones/116-campeon-2005 Sporting Cristal campeón 2005][https://rpp.pe/futbol/mas-futbol/recuerde-el-ultimo-titulo-nacional-obtenido-por-sporting-cristal-noticia-547651 Recuerde el último título nacional obtenido por Sporting Cristal] The season started on March 5, 2005, ended on December 21, 2005. ==Changes from 2004== ===Structural changes=== Starting with the 2004 season, the two relegated teams will be able to choose to play in the [[Peruvian Segunda División|Segunda División]] or drop to their regional league as the Segunda División will now be played with non-capital teams. The number of first division teams dropped from 14 to 13. ===Promotion and relegation=== [[Deportivo Wanka]] and [[Atlético Grau|Grau]]–[[Estudiantes de Medicina|Estudiantes]] finished the 2004 season in 13th and 14th place, respectively, on the three-season average table and thus were relegated to their regional league. They were replaced by the champion of the 2004 Copa Perú [[Club Sport Áncash|Sport Áncash]]. ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! Promoted from
